utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was it your aim it to disable the resettlement of Serbs in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was it one of your aims to exert continuous military pressure on the Vlasic-Jajce-Kupres line and the Travnik-Vecici-Kotor Varos line?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see how we could have contributed to that purpose. It was a wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, wish.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the wish of every citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in every citizen, I'm asking about you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was my wish, I would have really wanted Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, wait. Let's be very precise. It was your wish to exert continuous military pressure on the Vlasic-Jajce-Kupres line and the Travnik-Vecici-Kotor Varos line; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please to have an objective is one thing, an intimate desire is something else. Intimate desires are not up for discussion here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We'll come to intimate desires. Was it one of your aims or let's say intimate desires to conduct surveillance over prominent SDS members in some of the cities to contribute to your security?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's find a reminder then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. It's number -- yes, it's in e-court, 2D05-0047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document, the qualification of the witness's work or activities as clandestine, is that your qualification or is that the witness's qualification? You use it but do you have it from his book, or is it your qualification?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the answer is in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have the last page, please

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krzic, towards the bottom of the page, do we see your signature, Muharem Krzic, president of the Executive Board of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. In this correspondence between parties, you use this greeting Mahsuz Sellam, we discussed this before?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it does conclude with best regards, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It does. But please read to the Trial Chamber your own proposals. Point 1, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, will you allow me to add something to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, I won't. Let the Prosecutor allow you to do this.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then you read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't mind. In this document in point 1, does it say: "Urgent deployment of international military forces in Banja Luka." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Point 2, "media attention to Banja Luka and Bosanska Krajina." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My answer is going to be yes to all of these points if you read them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 3: "Establish a professional team to monitor the situation in Bosanska Krajina." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Point 4: "Prevent any form of Serb resettlement in Banja Luka." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 5: "Continuous military pressure on Vlasic-Jajce-Kupres and Travnik-Vecici-Kotor Varos" yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And point 6: "Keep an eye on prominent members of the SDS in some of the cities as a guarantee of our safety" yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we have this document as next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 2D31, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What was the dates, I forgot again?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we have the first page, please. The date is 11th of October, 1992. [Interpretation] Now do you remember, Mr. Krzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I'm sorry, but I didn't see the answer to my question in what you showed us. You said we would see it in this document, in the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't understand you, Your Honour. I was asking him to confirm these measures that he proposed to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, my question was -- my question was about the beginning of this line of questions. You said his activities -- his activities were clandestine. You qualified them as clandestine, and my question is, is that your qualification of his activities or is that the witness's qualification, in his book eventually?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I clarify that immediately, Your Honour, but this is another line of question but for the basis I'll establish immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Krzic, you heard the Judge, His Honour Judge Delvoie. You will agree with me if I say that based on all of your witness statements and your book and everything else, I came to the conclusion that you led a very proactive clandestine activity in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's partially true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It involved contacts with your own representatives, with foreign embassies, international representatives, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it wasn't clandestine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In those activities you use code-names, encryption, some secret science?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with the institutions you mentioned. It was exclusively used among members of the Executive Board of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to that. But you had a group that secretly gathered intelligence on the Army of Republika Srpska, the movements of troops, funerals of Serb soldiers, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in that group of yours, you used code-names?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was only between one other person and me. Just one other person and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you were the brain of the whole operation in the group?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the brain of the group. It was all spontaneous. Everything that was found out on the ground was transmitted to me reckoning that I would go abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you were at the head of this intelligence group?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And your code-name was Torry?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I started using that Tory code-name only towards the end of 1992 hoping that it would give me some protection. As for the other code-names, I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was your code word for weapons? Was it "timber"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It was only in the correspondence between another member and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the code word for danger was "heat"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I see you have information from the police who interrogated that group. What they told the police, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, all this is in your statements, but we'll come to that later. No need to defend yourself. That's your activity and you were convicted before a competent Court for that. But what I want to know about is the rally that the SDA organised in Banja Luka, and that was, correct me if I'm wrong, on the 20th April 1991. You remember that rally?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember the rally, but I would really have to look at my notes to confirm the date, but I take your word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's what you say in your book?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it must be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You say that renowned representatives of the Bosniak community from Zazine Krajina dared to come to the very nest of the Chetnik headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the derogatory term we used for hotel Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then President Alija Izetbegovic who attended the rally said the following: "We send a message to our neighbours that we will share both good and evil with them, but we will never again go with our heads bent and we will never again be second-class citizens. We offer them to build jointly a joint state." You remember these words by Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How do you understand these words? I didn't understand from your answers that Muslims used to be second-class citizens in Bosnia-Herzegovina. What is this supposed to mean in this context? In 1992 who was threatening the interests of the Bosniak people?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it had more to do with the historical context. Why? Primarily because Bosniaks as a people were unfortunately not recognised in the former Yugoslavia. They could declare themselves in the census as Muslims, but it was not our historical name, and I think these words by Izetbegovic refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You go on to say that the joint message was a unified integrated Bosnia-Herzegovina without creating nationally homogenous regions which would be against all the peoples, and it goes on to say, There would be no division of Bosnia except if someone wishes bloodshed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you are reading correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How did you interpret this statement he made, this remark that it may end in bloodshed? Was it a peacemaking speech, or was it a kind of brandishing of arms?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course as he was speaking, I was not able to analyse every word, but I think the general impression was very positive. There were Serbs also at the rally, there was a pretty loud applause in the second part of the rally, and this passage where Izetbegovic spoke about joint construction was welcomed by Mr. Abdic who clarified this economic part at least with regard to Bosnian Krajina. And then you should also know that Bosnia is a patchwork ethnically speaking, a leopard skin, and every attempt to create exclusive territories where there would be no room for others meant bloodshed because no one would accept it, and I think it ultimately turned out that what Mr. Izetbegovic said was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in 1991 armed forces were created under the name of Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But armed forces were established?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps only on paper. We also wanted to make supplies of medicines and bandages in case of war. Anyway, I was not informed of that, although I was permanently in Banja Luka at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right, but you did speak about the indivisibility of territories but you also said and confirmed that you wanted to form six new municipalities within the municipality of Banja Luka with a non-Serb majority. Isn't that contrary to what Izetbegovic is saying?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are forgetting to mention the formation of ZOBK the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and this referendum, and the SAO Krajina exclusively Serb creations. All this came before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You told us here that it was your initiative to create municipalities with a majority non-Serb population. You confirmed this for the record. It's documented. So I'm asking you now, isn't that contrary to your interpretation of Izetbegovic's speech, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. You use very often in your statements and in your writings the phrase that Banja Luka was a concentration camp?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would that be part of your literary writing, or is it a claim that Banja Luka was a concentration camp? Please hear me out. Do you agree that a concentration camp, as I understand it at least, from the tragic history of the Second World War should have armed security, should have a certain structure, and people within are destroyed? How do you explain that when Banja Luka was a place when there were planes and buses travelling from Banja Luka, international representatives were coming and going, life was going on, with all the incidents that also occurred I don't deny, isn't it -- isn't this literary language of yours that Banja Luka was a concentration camp a little bit exaggerated? Please don't -- this is cross-examination, just answer me with a -- was it an exaggeration?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you about the memory of the Second World War. The Warsaw ghetto was not a ghetto to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krzic, this is a cross-examination, please. I'm asking you on the basis of all I stated before, would you correct your statement now? Would you say that perhaps you were rather liberal in your estimate of the situation in Banja Luka, do you change your position or not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I allowed to say to which dates this refers because as far as 1992 and 1993 is concerned, I stand behind what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you mention genocide, do you know the legal definition of genocide, do you have the legal training to enable you to know what it is?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could explain that but that would take too much time, and it isn't necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your books and statements, you exaggerate some events and to do so for purposes of propaganda, that's why you mention genocide, concentration camps, extermination, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You did so for propaganda reasons to attract the attention of the international public; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have evidence to corroborate all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But that's not legal evidence, these are your assessments; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there is legal evidence among that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to define something here, namely, in your statements and in your book you mention that you were arrested by soldiers and taken to the CSB building in Banja Luka, later to Mali Logor in Banja Luka, do you remember those episodes?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And for the transcript and for the benefit of this case, I would like you to agree with me that this all was happening on September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not fully concentrated, so I'm not sure if it's September or early October, but I believe it was September 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During a military action, September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This was very important to me because all these events are outside of the scope of the indictment so we don't want to waste time on that and take it off the agenda. Now, about Banja Luka, let's clarify some issues. Number one, in your statement you say that the SDA, which party was dissatisfied with political life, to put it that way, that the SDA walked out of the Banja Luka Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To express their protest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Protest, yes. And that protest, the reason for that protest was the fact that out of 117 members of the Assembly, 68 voted in favour, that's a majority; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was a simple majority, a two-thirds majority was required.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please wait, I'm going step by step, we'll clarify everything. You are saying that the SDS then created a majority because they were able to get some votes from other parties; correct? Who do I have in mind specifically, the communists and your former Muslim Assembly member Mr. Emir Busatlic, that's what you say in your book, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The SDS, whatever parties, passed a majority decision about joining the association of communities -- sorry, municipalities of Bosnian Krajina. That was on the 1st of May 1991, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that decision was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then to express your protest, when I say you, I mean the SDA party, you walked out; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the procedure was illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Now, tell me your personal opinion. What was happening and how do you assess the procedure during the night between the 14th and 15th October 1991 in the Assembly of the Republic of BiH when the vital interests of the representatives of the Serbian people were jeopardized and when the Serbs were outvoted by the Muslims and Croats? Tell me, did that threaten the constitutional order, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the constitution that was in force at the time, and especially I'm not familiar with the rules of procedure of the then parliament of BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you remember that this caused a serious crisis after which a series of events ensued?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that event when the representatives of the Serb people left the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your contacts in Banja Luka, did you ever hear that the main motive was the unconstitutional outvoting of the Serb representatives?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably I did hear about it but I didn't interpret it that way because I wasn't familiar with the regulations -- laws and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, that we are speaking about the establishing of the Republika Srpska, you know that it was established by plebiscite in January 1992, and it came of age recently, you do know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the Republika Srpska adopted its constitution, subordinate legislation, and it established government soon afterward; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska as the the other part of Bosnia-Herzegovina which other part was subsequently called the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And that Federation was made up of the representatives of Croats and Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Serbs. I'm referring to the territory. The laws of former Yugoslavia were applied in both entities; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, but, sir, these are questions you should put to a legal expert. I am willing to answer them, but, well, as far as I remember constitution was adopted to the effect that the laws of the SFRJ should be taken over unless they are in collision with the new laws and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not a legal expert, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Now, do you know that during Ante Markovic's time in former Yugoslavia there were changes in the property structure and a lot of private companies were founded and there was economic expansion, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what people were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since you worked for Pliva in Zagreb, do you know that property was transformed into joint stock companies, you are familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And not being a lawyer, as you say, you cannot say for certain how many privately-owned companies there were in the territory of Banja Luka, and how much property transformation there was, et cetera? I'm saying this for the sake of the transcript, you are not a legal expert and you have no accurate information about the economic structure in Banja Luka at the time about which you are testifying?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did say that these -- that my assessment was approximate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, the assessment of a layperson; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just like your assessment of the mechanisms with regard to acquiring real property, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You may or may not know that in 1992 in the police, the military, the public administration, the health care, there were many non-Serb professionals and experts in high positions, and they were loyal citizens of the Republika Srpska, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know their numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that at the time and throughout the war -- or, I apologise for this remark, we will deal with this in our Defence case, but I must clarify some things with you here. Do you know that Dr. Ivor Komljenovic a Croat by ethnicity in 1992 and throughout the war was the head of the dialysis ward in the Banja Luka hospital?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that one prominent member of the government of the Republika Srpska after the war was Dr. Ivor Komljenovic who was the minister of health?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1992 until the end of June or maybe July 1992 Banja Luka was encircled and completely cut off militarily?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the disruption of communication around Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Until mid-1992, Banja Luka was surrounded by Croatian forces in the north; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I go into that, I must also remember the -- I must also mention the Knin Krajina --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But this isn't a trick question, Witness. Croatian forces were stationed in the north, so normally you couldn't go through Croatia. In the west there were the forces of the Army of BiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the south, Travnik and what you mentioned, there was also the Army of BiH, but also the forces of the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The corridor in the east was cut through partly by HVO forces in the Posavina and partly by the forces of the ABiH from Doboj toward Brod; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, then, Banja Luka at that time was totally isolated?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But as far as I know, there were routes for the supply of oil and medication, et cetera. I don't know whether you are familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the overall situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, it's that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sorry, sorry, I wasn't watching. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is coming in, I'd ask if I could raise one matter with you. The next witness, Victim Witness has returned him to his hotel because based on the projections it appears that we won't get to him before the end of the session today. I just wanted to advise you of that in case Your Honours wanted to take the position to tell Mr. Pantelic he had 15 more minutes and Mr. Olmsted has 5 minutes then I could call Victim Witness and say bring him back, if that's not the case then we'll just let him stay there and come tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. While the witness is returning to the stand, the Chamber is concerned that the times which have been projected by counsel, in some cases extended times, is not being efficiently and effectively used, and the fact that counsel on any side has been allotted a block of time doesn't mean that that time is to be spent on matters that are obviously irrelevant, and counsel -- with counsel to undertake excursions into matters which are at best of peripheral and tangential importance, and I remind counsel that the Chamber reserves the right notwithstanding the times which have been allotted by previous agreement to bring examination or cross-examination to an end as the case may be in order to move these matters forward as efficiently and effectively and progressively as they should be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krzic, before the break we spoke about Banja Luka being surrounded and about certain aspects of life in Banja Luka itself. Do you agree with me when I say that a huge number of refugees of Serb ethnicity, mostly from Croatia and other territories outside Banja Luka, to a significant extent impaired the normal functioning of the city?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Likewise, the presence of a great number of soldiers coming from the front line and some military operations greatly jeopardised the safety of the citizens of Banja Luka which you also mentioned in some statements of yours?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At the same time a military corps was deployed in Banja Luka, it was the 5th JNA Corps and later on it was renamed into the Krajina Corps commanded by General Talic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are not a military expert and neither am I, but I believe that the strength of that corps was about -- I've just been told about 100.000 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't go as far as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, if a brigade had from 3- to 5.000, it depends on the number of brigades in the corps. But anyway, we will agree that the Krajina Corps was a respectively military force which was deployed in the Bosnian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- well, it's common knowledge more or less, but do you know that on the 12th of May, the decision of the Presidency of the Republika Srpska was confirmed by the Assembly, and it was a decision about the existence of the imminent threat of war? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, but I'm not sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At any rate, we will certainly agree based on some information that we have that in this situation the imminent threat of war, the military factor assumes a great importance; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That applies to the process of mobilisation, the launching of certain procedures, and with regard to deserters and others so that military courts get a greater significance than in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Parts of your evidence, and you mentioned a detail in the marketplace when soldiers were behaving arrogantly toward non-Serb population, provoking people, et cetera, and you also say that soldiers blackmailed the owners of small businesses if they were not Serbs, do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that period, your personal activity and that of your party was directed toward indicating such incidents and that's why you contacted military officers very often?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very often. There were only two or three such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that period you also acted as an intermediary trying to influence the resolution of the situation in Kotor Varos. Tell us briefly what kind of activities those were and what made you get involved?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kotor Varos, as opposed to the situation in some other towns where I went sometimes, well, Kotor Varos wasn't a place that I didn't visit. In that latest incident, and we saw relevant document today, I was invited by Mr. Kupresanin immediately after I had met Mr. Galbraith, the US representative, and why did I agree to go to Kotor Varos? I believe I explained my reasons, but here they are anyway. I went there to monitor the surrender of those people who had put up resistance so as not to be slaughtered or taken away some place, if that will suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In other words, in the Kotor Varos municipality, there was fierce fighting between Muslim forces and Serb force; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were combined Muslim Croat forces fighting Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who commanded those Muslim Croat forces, do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first time I met the people who were the leaders of that resistance. That was the in the village of Vecici. In other areas, other people were in charge. I am speaking about three people, should I mention their names?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, do give me the name if you know.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three. One was Alagic, I don't know his first name. He was wearing an ABiH uniform, he got killed later, and two others didn't wear uniforms, the name of one was Hilmo or Necko. These are the three people I met, and not only me but also the others who were a member of that delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Muhamed Sadikovic the commander of that military unit in that zone of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see or meet him there. I only got to meet him later in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm merely asking because he is the co-author of your book and he describes the situation in great detail. But let's go on anyway. So you were a mediator in let's call it the safe departure from that territory, of course assisted by the national representatives, so the armed formation of the ABiH left the territory around Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my task to convince them, and not only me, but also the other members of that group, to convince them to surrender, to persuade them. Whatever I said, I said because I wanted to save human lives. My only role in that was the following: I said I didn't want to know about the military forces, their strength or any other details. I only insisted that international humanitarian organisations and foreign journalists be involved in the surrender, and I believe that's how it took place too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before your next question, I will interrupt to bring your attention to it's 12.44. You are required to complete your cross-examination by 1.30 at the very latest, and the remaining 15 minutes will be allowed to Mr. Olmsted to re-examine, so to be finished this witness by 1 -- in order to take the adjournment at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will agree probably, if you remember it, that these military operations in the territory of Kotor Varos lasted until May or June 1992 -- sorry, from May June 1992, until the autumn?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was there in October, that being still autumn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At that time you co-operated with and kept in touch with the commander of the Serbian forces, at that time Lieutenant-Colonel Bosko Peulic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's when I first met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In these contacts with him, what was your impression about him? Was he a man of authority in his area of responsibility, or was he just a part of the delegation? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without going into his actual powers in the chain of military hierarchy which I'm not familiar with, I thought, it was my impression, that he was a man of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the context of not Kotor Varos but the broader area, you speak of the attack by "our group Osa" consisting of saboteurs from Croatia which destroyed several aircraft in the area of Mahovljani, do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's an airfield near Banja Luka, right? Mahovljani.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this operation really happen?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the radio, I'm not sure about the television. We had constant blackouts, but there was a report on the radio, and I believe the newspapers wrote about it. It was on Radio Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was this Osa group? Was it an armed unit?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was obviously armed. We had not known anything about it until that report, and they were obviously sent from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were they arrested later? Did they manage to return to Croatia, or were they put on trial in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that any of them were arrested. I don't know of any trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Compared to the work of the SDA that is relative to the work of the SDA in the area of Bosnian Krajina, you mentioned several times that you met with your colleagues frequently or almost always in Prijedor because the SDA was in power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that's where you felt safe and you had all the freedom to conduct your party activities? Prijedor was your regional centre, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So why did you choose Prijedor for your frequent contact?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, they were not frequent. I think you can count on the fingers of one hand how many times I was in Prijedor. But sometimes those were meetings of the regional board. You were right, though, that we felt a little safer there, at least you were safe from surveillance by the police in wire-tapping, which was quite uncomfortable. So Prijedor was safer but it wasn't the base of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, the materials mention that there were a couple of thousand pieces of weapons in the area of Prijedor and even a light calibre cannon?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard about the same thing, but it could have been propaganda because it was well known that we were coming from Banja Luka and among all the members of the SDA there was a lack of security culture. All of them were laymen who were quite new to politics. Apart from me, very few people had any experience in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You personally, apart from the weapon that you mentioned, also owned a Beretta pistol?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a licensed pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You also had a 9-millimetre pistol?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refuse to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, what difference does it make, Mr. Krzic, whether you had one or not, it's the same thing? I mean, I really don't understand? You intrigue me now, what's the problem with that pistol? Was it perhaps involved in a crime? Did you wound or kill anyone?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never even fired it. But this Beretta was taken away from me although I had a licence and although I personally was shot at at my door-step and grenades fell as close as 20, 30 metres away from me, and I wanted to have some protection at least to die an honourable death if nothing else without suffering too much at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, although this is a bit outside of the period of the indictment, but it's still relevant to your situation, you said that when in September 1993 some people from the military arrested you and detained you, some police officers, although it's not certain whether they were real police officers or paramilitary, you said that these police officers regular or irregular saved you from that military detention?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: They snatched you out of that military prison and took you to some motel?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you confuse the beginning and the end. I thought you were talking about the beginning when I went through all sorts of torture that I described, and I still can't imagine how I managed to survive all that. After all this torture when I was already unconscious, suddenly two men burst into the building of the SUP, nowadays CSB, and dragged me down the stairs because I couldn't walk, hoisted me up on a chair, and whispered in my ear -- no, sorry, I got it wrong. None of them told me anything, but later when I was taken to the suburbs of Banja Luka in that car and when they dragged me out into that low building with all that electronic equipment and computers and radio stations, et cetera, one of them set me in a chair and said, Do you want to have a vodka? I replied, I thought you were going to execute me. And he answered, No, we come from Mr. Karadzic. We are here to save you. That's the whole story.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At any rate without going into all that detail, it was obviously a reason why you were under special protection in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found out to this day, although I think the reason lies in my exposure because I was visited by foreign journalists, foreign diplomats, and to this day I can't understand how it is that I stayed alive. I see that as God's will.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All this, Mr. Krzic, was going on in September 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As an intellectual, you are aware of certain criminal legal aspects and you have also done your military service and you've read literature. You know that there is such a crime as espionage?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Espionage as a crime in wartime under any system becomes an aggravated act as compared to peacetime?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I now wish to ask you, I think it was in 1991 when your son visited -- or rather, served in the military, did his military service Vinkovci and Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During his military service, you travelled with your family to visit him, and on your way back you noticed certain movements of JNA units?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were not JNA units, they were civilians wearing visor caps. Some of them were leather caps, they were rather close so I could see their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: They were members of which units?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know. They showed the three-finger sign which could have been a threat or a sign of support because my car had Banja Luka licence plates. It's difficult to guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your evidence you mentioned some place that going back through Croatia you telephoned a friend of yours with the initial T in Zagreb, and informed him of the movement of armoured units based in Zaluzani if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, did I not say anything about movement. I just told him these units had received lethal ammunition -- live ammunition, but that was in the context of the previous incident you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was all in the middle of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And where were the JNA armoured units stationed, the ones you mentioned to your friend in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zaluzani.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did you begin your intelligence work in Banja Luka? When did you decide to form this group to collect all sorts of information?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened quite spontaneously. But, in fact, the collection of information started much earlier because the International Red Cross and the high commissioner wanted us to report to them daily what is going on in Banja Luka and we did that. And all these reports that you may or may not have were given verbally or in writing to all the heads of these international organisations. However, when we begin to -- when we began to suspect that these reports that were sent suddenly to their head offices did not end up only in the hands of politicians, we began sending our own reports to all the addresses that we could find. Sometimes we sent them openly. The Serbian authorities deliberately allowed me to keep my telephone and my fax machine, and there was no doubt they were continuing to wire-tap both. And as you rightly say, when I had the report to make where the source was questionable, I sent it in different ways that I don't think I'm going to discuss here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's appropriate time to go into private session, due to the recent answer that we got. Just for a couple of minutes, I think, because he is about to reveal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is it relevant, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's relevant, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Relevant to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To the case. To the case here that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It doesn't appear to any of us on the face of it that it is. Can you indicate --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll move on. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We'll now look at your statement of 22nd -- 26th through 29th August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court, it's 2D06-0463.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this passage from your statement to come up, could you tell me this, I think it's also mentioned in your writings, namely that apart from your associates, there was also your wife in Zagreb who passed on this information?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was your son also involved?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He was not a member of the BH Army at the time, was he?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and he was not aware of these things. He was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand. So he did not respond to the mobilisation call-up?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How is he supposed to answer the mobilisation call-up? He did his military service in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 6 of your statement in Bosnian. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could just see the top of the page. Sorry, scroll down to see the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Krzic, should I give you the English version? It's not in dispute that you gave this statement; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph. Not to waste time reading it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just tell me, how does it begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph begins with the words: "Throughout my stay in Banja Luka, as long as I was in Banja Luka..." will you just confirm. It says that a simple gist of code words was devised for communication with Smajo Djuzel. For President Izetbegovic this is not a good translation. You used code name Babo or Dido. Bobo doesn't sound right. Babo is logical. Danger was called "heat" in your code language?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You had over 100 code words in your communication with Smajo Djuzel, maybe more?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very short list of code words, really, because we did not exchange much information, and I did not receive any significant information in this way, apart from some private reports about internal quarrels about -- among those people who stayed down there, no directives or anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you have lost me. I fail to see how this has any relevance to the trial. So please explain to me, make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, absolutely, I will give the grounds. Your Honour, Mr. Krzic, and we shall show the relevant documents at the end of line of these questions, in accordance with his previous statements and also the part of statement that he gave to OTP, was organiser and chief of network of intelligence group and finally members of these group and Mr. Krzic were persecuted, charged by the indictment of military Prosecutor and finally judgement was delivered. The point here is that we as Defence would like to show that any proceedings against Mr. Krzic or because he is rely about certain events in military and police and, you know, these services, was not arbitrary, number one. All these proceedings were in accordance with valid legislation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But that is not disputed. Point one, it's outside the scope of the indictment. Point two, nobody has challenged that Mr. Krzic was subsequently prosecuted and convicted for espionage. This is completely outside the interests to this trial. Unless you do it for the purpose of challenging the credibility of the witness, but in that case, please advise us as to which parts of his testimony in your view are unreliable because of the witness's, in your view, his unreliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. The theory of Prosecution case is that my client is responsible being a member or supporter or aider or abettor of joint criminal enterprise on a larger scale, not including just Bosanska Krajina and elsewhere. Part of the indictment is the -- that he through his omissions to work professionally and also as a form of prosecution, he denied basic rights of non-Serbs in this region through policy, acts you know, aiding and abetting procedure, and what we would like to show here through certain line of questions is that practically there were sufficient grounds for criminal proceedings and also this particular witness, he testified also in order to provoke international reaction, at a certain stage he created non-objective picture of events in Banja Luka and Banja Luka is a part of the indictment. So I would like to show through the facts and proofs here, including the criminal proceedings against Mr. Krzic, that the nature of his information which was disseminated and sent out of Banja Luka was of practically non-realistic to the situation and finally, the consequences that our client is facing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But, with respect, Mr. Pantelic, wouldn't that involve this Chamber going into -- in fact, conducting its own inquiry into the sufficiency or insufficiency of the charges that were laid against this witness? In turn, the farthest that you can go in terms of this trial is challenging, as Judge Harhoff has said, the credibility of this witness, and the Prosecution must be taken as a fact, we needn't go beyond that, because it would be wholly incompetent for this Chamber to be taken down the road where you seem to wish to take us, unless I'm wholly missing something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I absolutely accept your points. The issue here is that in terms of, as you well mentioned and already pointed out, the credibility of a witness also because to a certain line of questions and events in Banja Luka we got a number of answers from him, and also we, for the record, would like to have a fact that he was charged and he was finally convicted for his acts there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And there's no dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: In any case, Mr. Pantelic, before Mr. Olmsted replies, if I understand your point correctly, you are saying that the acts for which your client is charged were done partly in response to the misinformation that you hold that this witness was spreading in the relevant period, so if I understand you correctly, you say that this witness was participating in a campaign of misinformation to the outside world about the conditions in Banja Luka and other places, Prijedor, and for that reason the Serbian authorities had to react, and those reactions were justified? Is that your point of view?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour. As far as the events in Banja Luka concerned, we -- the position of Defence is the following: Banja Luka was in very specific conditions at this period of time, and as Mr. Krzic affirmed here and confirmed, a flow of refugee came to Banja Luka and security conditions were deteriorated and many incidents occurred, et cetera, et cetera. But the position of the Defence is to show two general things with regard to Banja Luka. Point number 1 is that on political level that we have discussed before, the, I would say, common agreement between ruling parties were to establish a political life, then creation of municipalities, then process of dissolution in Bosnia, et cetera, et cetera. That's one part of the background. The other parties that the theory of the Prosecution is that in pursuing the common purpose and joint criminal enterprise, my client created unbearable conditions for non-Serbs in Banja Luka, denying non-Serbs on fundamental rights, aiding and abetting in certain policies, et cetera, et cetera. So the position of the Defence is the following: We would like to get a particular number of answers from this witness with regard to the conditions in Banja Luka, events in Banja Luka, and ultimately persons in charge or players in Banja Luka. At the same time, at the same time, Your Honours, we are - that's our position - we are free to challenge credibility of this witness because we think that in order to -- to inflate propaganda against Serbs' actions, at least it was an exaggeration in terms of informations which was sent through official and unofficial ways by this witness and his group. And finally, Your Honour, if you allow me, if, and I don't think that that would be a case, if there is not any dispute from the Prosecution side with regard to the fact that Mr. Krzic was criminally charged, indicted, and finally convicted with regard to the criminal charge of espionage against the interest of Republika Srpska, et cetera, which is a part of this military Tribunal judgement, I don't have any problem to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes or no, Mr. Olmsted?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not contest that the witness was charged and convicted of espionage. Just let me make one note though, he was tried in absentia, which raises the issue that Your Honours are raising is how can you go into this trial -- his subtrial and bring it into this trial to be a whole another trial so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right, there we are. Mr. Pantelic, if you are seeking to elicit information from this witness about the conditions in Banja Luka during the period that is covered by the indictment, then get on with it. You have 11 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Krzic, for the sake of the transcript, it is not a contentious fact that you were sentenced by the military court in Banja Luka to 20 years in prison for espionage, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in absentia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it is also an undisputed fact that you with a group of members of your party engaged in activities to the end of organising armed groups which were supposed to rebel against the Serb authorities in Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you informed SDA headquarters that at a certain point in time, several thousand members of your armed unit would be ready to put up armed resistance in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never said anything of the kind. But I did say that if there should be mass slaughter that somebody will probably use a hidden weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When 3- or 4.000 people were driven into the Poljokono [phoen] park without any warning, and they were surrounded and the PA systems from police cars -- or from the PA systems from police cars we could hear the worst threats, such as, Turks, you will be killed here. On the same day there were a few killings at that very place. So the people were scared that the massacres from World War II would be repeated. I thought that at that moment, at such a moment, people would react with weapons, but they were on a clearing and probably the Serb authorities couldn't wait for something like that to happen, to retaliate. And the objective probably was to prevent [indiscernible] from coming to Banja Luka. But speaking about espionage, the high commissioner and the International Red Cross were immediately informed of the event and what I'm speaking about was not my idea. They were people who had experience who assessed that this was in fact a plot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. But let's go into this issue of the Muslim forces opposing the Serb forces. How many fighters did you have?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at my direct and indirect disposal, I didn't have any one fighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you said a minute ago that there were some illegal weapons ready to be used, I'm merely asking you how many fighters armed with those illegal weapons are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I received information about both the Serb side and the non-Serb side for various sources, but that doesn't mean that I had any leading role in that or I directed things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that, but I want to hear from you what the strength of that armed unit was?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that there were no more than 2.000 pieces of small calibre weapons in the hands of non-Serbs in Banja Luka, and I hasten to add, those were the figures of which I was informed by the Serb authorities, and I thought that they were probably correct. But that number includes hunting weapons too and there must have been hundreds around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. I can accept that as your view, but tell me now, Mr. Krzic, in these final questions, I consulted my client, and you mentioned that you saw Mr. Zupljanin in the Bosna hotel on the occasion of the meeting with Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen. Much time has elapsed, but my client says that he met Vance and Owen but in the office of Mr. Radic and the municipal building, the town hall. That the meeting didn't take place at the Bosna hotel. Do you think that might be right? Would you be willing to correct your statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received that piece of information from my co-workers. I couldn't be everywhere all the time. I was in a meeting with Mr. Karadzic and Krajisnik and Mr. Brdjanin. I couldn't see everything with my own eyes, but what matters is the press conference, which was public. So the commander of the CSB, if he wasn't present, he certainly received a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krzic, this is only for procedural clarification. Do you know that in 1992 in that campaign of uncertainty, feeling insecure with regard to the many members of military units or paramilitary units, do you know that explosive devices were placed under the cars of Mr. Radic; the mayor, a Serb; and Dr. Vukic, a prominent representative of the SDS also a Serb? Did you know that their property was also blown up, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, I know there was explosive placed under someone's car but I don't remember exactly because it's been quite some time. I would have to consult my book. I'm not a living encyclopedia, so I don't know all the details, but I think there were such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Krzic, in the examination-in-chief, there was discussion about the imposition of a curfew. Do you agree that curfew is a regular measure of safety and security in the situation of imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krzic, about the Crisis Staff, we learned that the SDA had its Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, yes, it was called that, but its function was something else altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm not speaking about the function. What matters to me is just the fact that there was an SDA Crisis Staff in Banja Luka and that the president of that Crisis Staff was Asim Jakelic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only for a few months. It was abolished later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, it's 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we give the floor to Mr. Olmsted, Mr. Pantelic, I would like to know if you wish to tender the statements of the witness into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I got the precise answers from him which is not disputed, so I will leave it like that. I mean, this particular -- that is not challenged, everything is consistent in his answers. Just one more question to finish, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Krzic, you are probably familiar with the fact that in Banja Luka during that transformation of that National Defence Council from about April 1992 the so-called War Staff of ARK was established. Have you heard about that in your contacts?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember that now. I only remember the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to verify that piece of information with you. By way of finishing, I would like to complete the picture. You say that in November 1991, the newspaper "Vecernji List" published a story about the establishment of new municipalities in Majdan and Ivanjska which was organized by the HDZ. Can you tell us now whether there were such activities, is the majority of the population Croatian there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that I was not acquainted with either the boundaries of those future municipalities. I don't remember that at all. Apart or except what you mentioned today about Centar about which I had some information. And I spoke about that here. As for Ivanjska, I cannot tell whether the Croats there would have been a majority or whether their share would have been fifty/fifty. There were some Serbs there, but I don't know whether there were any Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I accept that but for the stake of the transcript let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Krzic, I only have 15 minutes, so please keep your answers very very brief. Can you tell us what was the function of the SDA Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only function was humanitarian, and I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No need to explain. Now, in your prior testimony, you explained that the non-Serb parties opposed the creation of the community of Bosnian Krajina municipalities also known as ZOBK. Can you tell us from the perspective of the non-Serb parties, how did the creation of ZOBK relate to this concept of a greater Serbian state?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the most important thing is that in the process of uniting these municipalities, I think there were 22, and there were some people who took part in that who we called them traitors, but 99 per cent of them were Serbian representatives, and representatives of other ethnicities didn't take part in that, and another striking example that the establishment of the ZOBK was conducted without regard to statutory or constitutional or other provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let me pause you there. I want to bring you back on track. My question is how is this Z-o-b-k, ZOBK creation related to the concept of there's going to be one giant Serb controlled state, how did it relate to that or how did it justify your fears in that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I mean, it was never raised in cross-examination this concept of greater Serbia state, and this stuff is completely out of the scope of cross-examination. Maybe my learned friend can ask Mr. Krzic what was the process of voting, what was the statutory provisions, but it's pure speculation. I mean, greater state, stuff like that, I mean it's absolutely out of the scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, the whole purpose of this line of questioning is relating to this -- the time that the cross-examination -- the Defence counsel spent cross-examining on the issue of this newly created Muslim municipalities in Banja Luka and so we need to go back a little bit in time to understand it and put it into context. If the Trial Chamber feels that it's irrelevant, this concept of creating these or this argument that these Muslim municipalities were being created, then perhaps I don't have to pursue this line of questioning, but this is the only witness who can really talk about this that is currently on the Prosecution 65 ter Exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You should focus your question on the questions -- the way that was specifically asked in cross-examination without trying to set any context because we'll never finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Were you, Mr. Krzic, were you aware of the decision to create the Autonomous Region of Krajina in September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we learned about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Was Banja Luka a member of this newly created ARK?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately. Only after 15 days because in the first vote they were unable to push it through.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, did the SDA and the non-Serb parties participate in the creation of this ARK?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't participate even if we had wanted to. After the statements given by the highest ranking officials of the SDS, I remember Mr. Kupresanin's statement to the effect that all SAO Krajinas would be united into a great Serbian state up to the border, the border of which will be the line Karlobag, Cijena you know those stories and there was even mention of Djevdjelija. Before the establishment of the ZOBK and in the process, we never gave our support.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you were shown your own statement that was recorded or reported in the "Glas" newspaper. I think it's 1D03-0156. And at the beginning of that statement, you talk about statements made by Radoslav Vukic. Can you tell us what political position Mr. Vukic held around this time-period?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vukic, as far as I know, was a member of the Executive Board of the SDS from the very beginning. Then at some stage he became the SDS leader. There was frequent rotation in high positions there. I believe even without Assembly sessions. Then he was a member of the Crisis Staff of Banja Luka on the regional staff and he was member of the Executive Board, I think it was called, of the RBK. And then the director of the medical centre, that is to say all medical services.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Were you aware that he was a co-ordinator for the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, again I don't see how this comes out of the cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, this let me have my five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: First of all, it's a leading question, it's not proper, and I don't believe that Mr. Vukic was at any point part of the cross-examination in that respect. Except his name was mentioned once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, it ties into again to the same issue. This document was shown to him, if I'm given a little bit of discretion for the next five minutes, I think I'll make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry again, it's a leading question, and this document pertains only to the creation of these municipalities in the municipality of Banja Luka. And that was the point of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted, please so confine yourself to what came out of cross-examination specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Why did the non-Serb political parties feel it was necessary to form municipalities within Banja Luka that were not Serb dominated?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the vein hope that in that way they would be able to survive in that small territory the size of some 5 or 6 square kilometres, that they would be able to preserve their presence and survive. Because what can you achieve if you have power in two municipalities? They are the lowest level of government. What can they do? They can -- they have jurisdiction about demolishing houses, they have jurisdiction over the routes of roads to be built, that's more or less it. Everything else was fictitious. Municipalities have no political influence or responsibility at any higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: What happened to this initiative to create new municipalities within Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting was held which was attended by Serbs, Croats, and Bosniaks on an equal footing. And speaking about municipality Stari Grad, the number of representatives in the Assembly, there were 17 Serbs, 13 Bosniaks, and 6 Croats, something along those lines. There was a Serb majority, as you can see, but not an absolute majority. And that was the headline in the newspapers too. The municipality of Stari Grad - miniature Bosnia. But the initiative fell through because that should have been the beginning of a subsequent procedure. What was required was the approval of the population of the local communities. But then in the next step, the approval of the municipality of Banja Luka was required where the Serbs were the majority. And the following step is this had to be forwarded to the cabinet and then by parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So except for this initial proclamation, it was embryonic. So it had no effect. And but you can tell by the names of the representatives that all ethnicities took part in that. It was at a time when that terrible nationalism hadn't yet gotten the better.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let me ask you one final question. Were there ever any plans by the non-Serb political parties to implement this initiative through forceful take-over of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, sir, you are Prosecutor, but how can you come up with such a question? It's totally unrelated. There are plenty of arguments to corroborate that, I don't need to go into them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just please answer the question. Was there any plans by the SDA or the other non-Serb parties to try to push this initiative through using any kind of force? Physical force.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that I must correct you, not only non-Serb political parties participated, there were also multiethnic parties with a Serb domination, such as the SDP and the reformist party so you should reformulate your question, but my answer would be no, there were only verbal attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krzic, for your attendance here and assisting the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home. We take the adjournment now to resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning in Courtroom I, I believe. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of January, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.
